_comment: Worked example of a PollyArranger registry — the single source of truth (see docs/02-data-model.md). This is VALID JSON (no // comments); annotations use _comment fields and are ignored by the loader. It shows five items spanning the whole state machine: one MERGED, one in a fix loop (RE_REVIEW), one freshly BUILDING, one BLOCKED on a human decision, and one still PLANNED.

policy._comment: Global pipeline policy. merge=human means Polly parks finished items and waits; it never auto-merges. maxReviewRounds caps fix->review loops before escalating. concurrency caps items building/reviewing at once.

waves.label: WAVE1
waves.goal: make the in-world lobby feel alive for the Sunday launch

waves.label: WAVE2
waves.goal: build-up announced publicly; discoverability + admin tooling

items._comment: MERGED — the happy-ish path with one blocking round. Mirrors the real p8 (github stars). Note implementer=claude_code, reviewer=codex (different family), reviewRound=2 (one fix loop), and the recorded review verdict CLEAN.
items.title: GitHub stars badge + star-history + live home pill
items.spec: Add a stars badge to README, a Star History chart, and a home-page stars pill that live-fetches the GitHub star count with caching + a graceful fallback.

items._comment: RE_REVIEW — currently in a fix loop. Reviewer (codex) raised BLOCKING findings round 1; implementer (claude_code) pushed fixes; codex is re-checking. Same vendors are sticky across rounds. The findings array is the structured review output the state machine branched on.
items.title: LLM lobby population layer (NPC peers)
items.spec: Add >=10 LLM-driven NPC peers that join the lobby room over the real WS protocol, wander, and chat. Off by default; prod-safe; free models with graceful degrade.

findings.what: welcome-id self-chat; enforce :free model + strip emoji

caveats: live LLM gen not verified headlessly — needs OPENROUTER_API_KEY

items._comment: BUILDING — just started. Roles assigned, worktree created off a known base, but no PR yet (pr=null) and no review yet. The implementer agent is editing files right now.
items.title: WAVE indicator -> inline ADMIN control
items.spec: Make wave assignment an inline admin-only control (click-to-change, no modal); assignable on unset items; public sees the label only. Must stay admin-gated.
caveats: backend wave-only PATCH already exists (PR#52) — must stay admin-gated (PR#50 isWorldAdminEmail)

items._comment: BLOCKED — good work, but waiting on a HUMAN decision, not a code failure. This is distinct from ABANDONED. The open question is recorded so the human can find exactly what needs their input. Mirrors the real onboarding email-gate 'wallet fork'.
items.title: Forced profile onboarding + email-verify gate on community
items.spec: Require profile completion on first run and hard-gate chat/community behind a verified email.
items.blockedOn: OPEN DECISION: wallet-only users have no Identity email -> can't be email-verified. Must they also create an email login / be exempt / accept lockout? Needs user decision before build proceeds.

items._comment: PLANNED — exists in the backlog, nothing assigned yet. The orchestrator will pick it up when a concurrency slot frees, assign roles (implementer != reviewer, different family), create the worktree, and move it to BUILDING.
items.title: Roadmap countdown header
items.spec: Add a countdown header to the roadmap page, consistent with the WAVE1 countdown pill styling.

notes._comment: The operator log (see docs/02-data-model.md section 5). Free-text, timestamped, typed. This is the human-readable catch-up trail and the highest-value record of WHY things happened — including mistakes.
notes.text: p8 merged (#56) after 1 blocking round (off-by-one n<0 vs n<=0 in star count caught by codex). Wave1.
An earlier item enabled the legacy 2.5D sprite crowd in the lobby — WRONG (project uses voxel avatars). User angry. Correction filed as a new revert item; keep this note for the post-mortem.
p10 blocked on wallet-email fork — awaiting user decision (see item.blockedOn).
Merge order set: p0 -> p1 -> p2 already done; next p6 + p7 -> cross-review -> human merge. merge-gate is the bottleneck (by design).
